parsed.why: Death-penalty exposure for same-sex activity, documented escalating flogging, security forces pursuing trans women, and abuse by family and militia with no protective framework. Severe risk on every axis.

Decriminalised with no documented state targeting of trans people and a tolerant society. Trans-specific evidence is thin: one undated account, no legal gender recognition, and labour protection excluding gender identity.

Passed bill would impose up to three years for identifying as transgender and require reporting, with assent pending. Mob violence and community raids are documented. Trans visitors face a looming trans-specific criminal offence.

Article 489 is applied to trans people, and police forced a suspect to show genitals and filmed and publicised an arrested cross-dresser's ID. Moral-charge enforcement, official hostility, and documented street-level violence add to this.

Consensual same-sex conduct is only read down, not repealed, and the statute still applies to trans-presenting people. Police dismissed anti-gay violence, and there is no trans-specific record. Hostility was aimed at gay tourists, and the 2014 non-enforcement statement mitigates somewhat.
